newsitem.title: UK: LVMH seeks arbitration on Guinness merger.
newsitem.headline: LVMH seeks arbitration on Guinness merger.

text.p: LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton AS said Friday it asked the International Chamber of Commerce to arbitrate its dispute with Guinness Plc over the proposed merger between Guinness and Grand Metropolitan Plc.
French drinks and luxury goods company LVMH is the biggest shareholder in Guinness, with a 14.2 percent stake, and has opposed the planned merger.

The company wants the chamber to decide if the deal, announced in May, represents a change of control at Guinness. The arbitration concerns a dispute over whether the merger constitutes a "control event" under the terms of agreements between LVMH and Guinness.
Meanwhile, Guinness said LVMH's move to seek arbitration lacked any legal basis.

"Guinness is clear that LVMH's claim that the proposed merger of GrandMet and Guinness would constitute a 'control event' lacks any legal basis, and is confident that the ICC (International Chamber of Commerce) arbitration will find accordingly," said the company in a statement.
LVMH argues that under the terms of agreements signed with Guinness, a "control event" would enable LVMH to operate its joint ventures with Guinness independently.
The company has argued that the terms would also allow it to market Guinness brands in key markets like the United States and the Far East for up to 10 years.
